title: AMD vs. Intel | Q3 2026 earnings calls
author: Daniel Nenni
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Intel was still larger in Q3, but AMD grew more than twice as fast and guided to a higher Q4 revenue midpoint. Both companies reported strong data-center demand. AMD expects its Helios AI systems and EPYC server chips to drive another step up in sales, while Intel is working to produce enough Xeon chips to meet demand as its PC business slows.

Data-center figures reflect each company’s own segment definitions. ir.amd.com

AMD’s growth is increasingly concentrated in data centers. EPYC CPUs and Instinct GPUs both contributed to the record quarter. The next step is shipping Helios racks in volume, alongside the ramp of its Venice server CPUs. On the call, management said it expects data centers to account for more than 80% of 2027 revenue, up from roughly 64% this quarter. AMD’s combined Client and Gaming segment fell 8%, even as client revenue rose 7%, because gaming revenue fell 40%. ir.amd.com
Intel’s AI demand showed up most clearly in Xeon. Management pointed to strong server CPU demand and an expanded Oracle collaboration, but cited manufacturing and packaging constraints on how quickly it can increase shipments. Intel expects the PC slowdown to last at least through the first half of 2027. A factory shutdown in Israel also contributes to the projected Q4 margin drop. intc.com
The next quarter will test whether AMD can turn early Helios deployments into volume shipments and whether Intel can turn unmet Xeon demand into sales while stabilizing margins. ir.amd.com

AMD into 2027. Management said on the call that it expects total revenue to grow more than 80% in 2027, with data centers accounting for about 80% of sales. That outlook depends on scaling Helios AI racks and Venice server CPUs. High-bandwidth memory supply is one constraint to watch. www.reuters.com

Intel into 2027. Management expects strong server CPU demand to continue, but supply could be tighter in the first half than in the second. Intel also expects the PC slowdown to last at least through the first half. The Israel factory shutdown adds pressure to Q4 margins, and Intel’s CFO expects little carryover from that incident into 2027 margins.
